subject: Urgent: client streaming parser metastability causing tail latency and 503s
messages:
From: Marcus Lowe <marcus.lowe@veridianhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, support@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Live ingest stalls — repeated 503s and high tail latency

Hi Jonas / Redwood support,

We're seeing repeated stalls in our live ingest pipeline this morning. Since ~08:45 PDT our customers started hitting intermittent 503s and a very high tail latency (p95 -> 6s, p99 -> 18s) when using the Redwood client SDK (js-sdk v2.1.3) for streaming inference. The failures coincide with chunked-transfer responses — the stream drops mid-header occasionally and the client then retries, which amplifies load.

I'm attaching a short sample_trace.txt with a few request IDs and a clipped HTTP trace showing the server sent a trailing header split across frames. We pushed only a config change overnight (batch size -> 16), but saw the issue before and after the change.

Impact: ongoing production errors for our checkout flows, several customer-reported timeouts. We need a mitigation ASAP — if there's a quick server-side or client workaround we can apply, please let us know.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lowe
VP Product, Veridian Health
marcus.lowe@veridianhealth.com

Attachment: sample_trace.txt (log snippet)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lowe <marcus.lowe@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-21T09:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Live ingest stalls — repeated 503s and high tail latency

Marcus — thanks for the quick report and the trace. We're looking at this as P1. A few quick Qs while we triage:

- Can you confirm whether you're using the streaming chat endpoint or the raw token stream?
- Are the clients behind a proxy/load balancer that might be re-chunking responses?
- Approx traffic during the incident (rps / concurrent streams)?

Immediate mitigations we can try from your side:
- Force the client into non-chunked mode (sets dechunking off) — I'll paste a one-line workaround if you want to try it now.
- Fallback to short-polling for the critical checkout path while we investigate.

I'll escalate to our streaming runtime team and loop in Sean and Soojin for a deeper dive. Sorry for the disruption — we'll prioritize a fix and propose a safe maintenance window if we need to apply a host-side hotfix.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Attachment: (none)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-21T10:02:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: Veridian — streaming parser instability (logs attached)

Sean / Soojin — forwarding Marcus's trace. Quick summary of what our telemetry shows:

- Spikes of 503s correlated with sustained concurrent streams from Veridian's prod region.
- A non-trivial fraction of failed responses show trailing header bytes arriving split across two chunk frames; the client dechunker occasionally fails to reassemble headers correctly and raises a parsing error, triggering immediate retry logic.
- Retries cause a short-lived overload on certain serving pods, which cascades into higher p99 across shared pools.

Attached: trace_chunklog.jsonl (stream of frame boundaries + header offsets), heap-prof.txt (sample heap dump from an affected pod).

Initial suspicion: a metastable dechunker state in js-sdk v2.1.3 where an off-by-one in the header buffer length check can drop the leading CRLF and leave the parser in a state where nextFrame processing treats the begins-of-header bytes as body. That would produce the exact symptoms Marcus reported.

Ask: can you triage and confirm whether the bug is client-only or we need a server-side defensible fallback (server coalescing of headers, stricter per-connection backpressure)? If it's client-only, we should push an emergency patch to the SDK and provide a short workaround for key customers. If server-side mitigations help us buy time, propose them; I'd like a recommended mitigation in the next 2 hours so I can coordinate with Veridian.

-JW

Attachments: trace_chunklog.jsonl, heap-prof.txt

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-21T14:18:00Z
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Veridian — streaming parser instability (logs attached)

I've reproduced a failing sequence in a local harness that mirrors the chunk boundaries from Marcus's trace. Summary of findings:

- Confirmed: js-sdk v2.1.3 dechunker has a state machine bug when a header block ends exactly at the boundary of a chunk and the next chunk begins with a single CR byte. The check that validates header termination expects CRLF in the same buffer and fails if CR is split.
- When the dechunker fails, it consumes part of the body as header continuation on the next frame, leading to a parse exception and an immediate retry from the client's reconnection code.

Temporary mitigations (safe):
- Server-side: enable header coalescing for streaming responses on affected pools (this merges chunk frames before sending to clients). This should reduce the probability of split-CR sequences. I can enable this on a subset of pods right away (no restart).
- Client-side (workaround): set env var REDWOOD_SDK_DECHUNK_STRICT=false or upgrade to patched js-sdk 2.1.4-rc which we will publish in the next hour.

Recommended action plan:
1) Enable server header-coalescing on Veridian's serving pool immediately (I can toggle flags and monitor).
2) Ask Veridian to set REDWOOD_SDK_DECHUNK_STRICT=false for now, or patch to 2.1.4-rc as a follow-up.
3) Prepare a host-side hotfix if coalescing is insufficient; I've drafted a hotfix_plan.pdf that outlines rollback and canary steps.

I'll prepare a short release of 2.1.4-rc and a quick KB article for customers with reproduction + workaround. Please confirm if I should proceed with enabling coalescing on the production pool.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior SWE, Runtime
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: hotfix_plan.pdf

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lowe <marcus.lowe@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-21T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Live ingest stalls — repeated 503s and high tail latency

Marcus — thank you for your patience and the detailed traces. Update and proposed next steps: 

What we found: our runtime engineer reproduced the issue and traced it to a corner-case in the JS client dechunker (js-sdk v2.1.3) where headers split across chunk boundaries can leave the parser in an inconsistent state. This is triggering client-side retries that cascade into pod overload and elevated p99/p99.9 latency.

Immediate mitigations we're ready to perform now (no service restart required):
- I can enable header coalescing on the serving pool handling your traffic (should reduce split-header events).
- On your side, if you can set REDWOOD_SDK_DECHUNK_STRICT=false for your deployment, it will avoid the strict check that is failing and reduce errors.

Planned next steps (safety-first):
- Soojin will publish a 2.1.4-rc patch in the next hour to fix the dechunker; we recommend you coordinate a quick rollout to your fleets after smoke tests.
- If coalescing doesn't sufficiently mitigate, we will schedule a short maintenance window to apply a host-side patch (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with rollback. I attached the hotfix_plan.pdf that outlines the canary plan and rollback criteria.

Compensation and accountability: we understand the impact and will offer a one-time credit against next month's usage for this incident. We'll also share the post-incident root cause analysis once the patch is out.

Please reply with: (1) permission to enable coalescing on your serving pool now, and (2) whether you can toggle the env var or prefer we wait for the 2.1.4-rc rollout. We can coordinate a short call if you'd like us on the line during the mitigation.

Apologies again — we aim to get this fully resolved within the next 24 hours.

Thanks,
Jonas
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
